title: What Is a Load Balancer?
sources: Akamai / Linode, 'Load Balancing Fundamentals: How Load Balancers Work': a load balancer sits in front of a group of servers and distributes incoming client requests across them; round robin sends requests to each server in turn; least connections sends a request to the server with the fewest active connections; health checks detect failed servers and stop sending them traffic

DesignGurus, 'Load Balancing Algorithms' guide: round robin cycles through servers in order; least connections picks the server currently handling the fewest connections; clients see a single address while many servers sit behind the load balancer

lines.text: but who decides which chef cooks each order?
Picture a manager at the kitchen door.
Every order goes to him first,
and he hands it to a chef.
The simplest way is taking turns,
one, two, three, then back to one.
Smarter ones pick the chef with the fewest orders.
And if a chef gets sick,
he stops sending that chef any,
your request hits the load balancer,
and it picks a healthy server for you.
One door outside, lots of servers inside.
